claims.evidence: This claim is supported by survival data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Acute morbidity in KC-RIK-shArid1a mice was closely associated with high degree of chimerism (>95%).
claims.source: Acute morbidity was closely associated with KC-RIK-shArid1a mice exhibiting a high degree of chimerism (>95%) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), indicating that at some level normal unrecombined cells can compensate for the gross functional defects produced by Arid1a depletion in this context.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Normal unrecombined cells can compensate for the gross functional defects produced by Arid1a depletion.
claims.source: Acute morbidity was closely associated with KC-RIK-shArid1a mice exhibiting a high degree of chimerism (>95%) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), indicating that at some level normal unrecombined cells can compensate for the gross functional defects produced by Arid1a depletion in this context.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that only high chimerism mice became moribund.

claims.claim: Moribund KC-RIK-shArid1a mice exhibited marked steatorrhea.
claims.source: Moribund mice exhibited marked steatorrhea (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating exocrine insufficiency as a possible cause of their failure to thrive.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Steatorrhea indicates exocrine insufficiency as a possible cause of failure to thrive in KC-RIK-shArid1a mice.
claims.source: Moribund mice exhibited marked steatorrhea (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating exocrine insufficiency as a possible cause of their failure to thrive.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the known relationship between steatorrhea and exocrine insufficiency.

claims.claim: Arid1a knockdown induces dramatic remodeling of the exocrine pancreas with replacement by Alcian Blue, Sox9, and Cytokeratin 19 positive mucinous metaplastic lesions.
claims.source: Consistent with decreased exocrine function, histological analyses revealed that Arid1a knockdown induces a dramatic remodeling of the exocrine pancreas compared to shRen mice. shArid1a exocrine parenchyma was predominantly replaced by Alcian Blue, Sox9, and Cytokeratin 19 positive mucinous metaplastic lesion (MMLs) (Figure 2B–D), characteristic of low-grade PanIN lesions (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figures 2B-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: The increase in PanINs upon Arid1a knockdown was accompanied by a dramatic reduction in cells positive for the differentiated acinar cell marker Cpa1.
claims.source: This increase in PanINs was accompanied by a dramatic reduction in cells positive for the differentiated acinar cell marker Cpa1 (Figure 2E,F), indicating a role for Arid1a in maintaining acinar cell identity in the setting of mutant Kras.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claims.claim: Arid1a plays a role in maintaining acinar cell identity in the setting of mutant Kras.
claims.source: This increase in PanINs was accompanied by a dramatic reduction in cells positive for the differentiated acinar cell marker Cpa1 (Figure 2E,F), indicating a role for Arid1a in maintaining acinar cell identity in the setting of mutant Kras.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed loss of acinar markers upon Arid1a suppression.

claims.claim: Acinar cell depletion upon Arid1a knockdown was likely a consequence of accelerated acinar ductal reprogramming rather than acinar cell death.
claims.source: Indeed, acinar cell depletion was likely a consequence of accelerated acinar ductal reprogramming rather than acinar cell death, since pancreata derived from shArid1a mice were not atrophied (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D), and showed similar levels of cleaved caspase three and Ki67 staining as controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data showing no atrophy and similar apoptosis/proliferation markers.

claims.claim: Only 1 of 11 KC-RIK-shArid1a mice that survived past 1 year showed histological evidence of PDAC at time of sacrifice.
claims.source: Of note, the Alcian blue-positive PanINs induced upon Arid1a silencing maintained low levels of Arid1a even after a year on dox chow (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C). Only 1 of 11 KC-RIK-shArid1a mice that survived past 1 year showed histological evidence of PDAC at time of sacrifice (Figure 2A), similar to historically reported rates of PDAC development in mice harboring Kras mutations in the absence of additional genetic events (Hingorani et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data from long-term survival studies.

claims.claim: The rate of PDAC development in KC-RIK-shArid1a mice is similar to historically reported rates in mice harboring Kras mutations alone.
claims.source: Only 1 of 11 KC-RIK-shArid1a mice that survived past 1 year showed histological evidence of PDAC at time of sacrifice (Figure 2A), similar to historically reported rates of PDAC development in mice harboring Kras mutations in the absence of additional genetic events (Hingorani et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This claim compares the current data to published literature.

claims.claim: While the ability of Arid1a to stabilize acinar cell identity may act as a barrier to pancreatic cancer initiation, other factors are likely necessary to promote the PanIN-to-PDAC transition.
claims.source: Thus, while the ability of Arid1a to stabilize acinar cell identity may act as a barrier to pancreatic cancer initiation, other factors are likely necessary to promote the PanIN-to-PDAC transition.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that PanINs do not progress to PDAC at high rates.

claims.claim: Acute loss of Arid1a in the setting of a pre-existing Kras mutation rapidly perturbs the identity and function of pancreatic acinar cells.
claims.source: Collectively, our data suggest that acute loss of Arid1a in the setting of a pre-existing Kras mutation rapidly perturbs the identity and function of pancreatic acinar cells, enhancing their sensitivity to metaplastic and PanIN-inducing signals stemming from oncogenic Kras.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claims.claim: C-RIK-shArid1a mice (without KrasG12D) did not become moribund following doxycycline administration.
claims.source: To this end, we eliminated the LSL-KrasG12D allele from ES cell-derived KC-RIK-shArid1a and KC-RIK-shRen mice though one round of breeding. These C-RIK-shRNA mice were then placed on dox at five weeks of age, after the completion of pancreas development, as in the KC-RIK experiments. In contrast to settings involving oncogenic Kras, these mice did not become moribund following dox administration, and pancreata from both shArid1a and shRen mice appeared normal (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Pancreata from C-RIK-shArid1a mice (without KrasG12D) appeared normal despite Arid1a suppression.
claims.source: In contrast to settings involving oncogenic Kras, these mice did not become moribund following dox administration, and pancreata from both shArid1a and shRen mice appeared normal (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: C-RIK-shArid1a mice retained expression of the acinar marker Cpa1 despite Arid1a knockdown.
claims.source: Importantly, shArid1a mice harboring wild-type Kras retained expression of the acinar marker Cpa1 (Figure 3E,F), which was lost in the KrasG12D setting.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claims.claim: No differences in markers of stressed acinar cells (Clusterin) or proliferation (Ki67) were noted in C-RIK-shArid1a mice compared to controls.
claims.source: Similarly, no differences in markers of stressed acinar cells (Clusterin) or proliferation (Ki67) were noted (Figure 3E,G,H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 3E, 3G, and 3H.

claims.claim: Arid1a is dispensable for maintenance of normal acinar cell identity.
claims.source: Although subtle differences in cell morphology and the pattern of E-cadherin staining were noted in cells with reduced Arid1a levels, no pancreas degeneration or exocrine insufficiency was observed despite sustained Arid1a knockdown. Therefore, Arid1a is dispensable for maintenance of normal acinar cell identiy (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data from long-term Arid1a suppression in the absence of Kras mutation.

claims.claim: Arid1a suppression had no impact on caerulein-induced pancreatitis damage and regeneration program.
claims.source: Arid1a suppression had no impact on this damage and regeneration program. At day two post-caerulein treatment, both C-RIK-shRen mice and C-RIK-shArid1a animals exhibited a similar increase in inflammation, ADM, and expression of acinar stress response genes (clusterin) and a concomitant decrease in expression of markers of acinar differentiation (Cpa1) (Figure 3J; and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C). Importantly, both inflammation and ADM were resolved to a similar degree by day nine in both genotypes (Figure 3—figure supplements 2A–C and 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data from caerulein-induced pancreatitis experiments.

claims.claim: Arid1a function plays a genotype-specific role in dictating acinar cell identity.
claims.source: Thus, Arid1a function plays a genotype-specific role in dictating acinar cell identity. It is dispensable for restoring normal acinar differentiation following transient tissue damage and dedifferentiation, but plays an active role in preventing preneoplastic lineage specification driven by oncogenic Kras.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing Arid1a effects in different genetic contexts.

claims.claim: Arid1a is dispensable for restoring normal acinar differentiation following transient tissue damage and dedifferentiation.
claims.source: Thus, Arid1a function plays a genotype-specific role in dictating acinar cell identity. It is dispensable for restoring normal acinar differentiation following transient tissue damage and dedifferentiation, but plays an active role in preventing preneoplastic lineage specification driven by oncogenic Kras.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the caerulein regeneration experiments.

claims.claim: Arid1a plays an active role in preventing preneoplastic lineage specification driven by oncogenic Kras.
claims.source: Thus, Arid1a function plays a genotype-specific role in dictating acinar cell identity. It is dispensable for restoring normal acinar differentiation following transient tissue damage and dedifferentiation, but plays an active role in preventing preneoplastic lineage specification driven by oncogenic Kras.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the differential effects of Arid1a suppression in Kras mutant vs wild-type contexts.

claims.claim: Previous work using traditional conditional mouse models showed that SWI/SNF subunits, when deleted concurrently with Kras activation, lead to decreased acinar sensitivity to Kras driven ADM and PanIN development.
claims.source: Our results showing that Arid1a suppression accelerates Kras driven erosion of acinar identity are surprising in light of previous work using traditional conditional mouse models in which SWI/SNF subunits, when deleted concurrently with Kras activation, lead to decreased acinar sensitivity to Kras driven ADM and PanIN development (Kimura et al., 2018; von Figura et al., 2014a).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: KC-RIK-shArid1a mice from the P5 cohort showed an accelerated reduction of acinar cells and increase in mucinous lesions resembling the adult phenotype.
claims.source: KC-RIK-shArid1a mice from the P5 cohort showed an accelerated reduction of eosinophilic acinar cells and a concomitant increase in mucinous lesions that were morphologically consistent with low grade-PanINs, resembling the adult phenotype (Figure 4C–E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: KC-RIK-shArid1a mice from the E7 cohort exhibited a striking retention of Cpa1+ acinar tissue.
claims.source: In contrast, KC-RIK-shArid1a mice from the E7 cohort, while still displaying ADM/PanIN lesions, exhibited a striking retention of Cpa1+ acinar tissue (Figure 4C–E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), a feature that was not observed in either P5 or adult cohorts.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The retained acinar cells in the E7 cohort failed to upregulate the ductal markers CK19 and Sox9 in the presence of mutant Kras.
claims.source: Moreover, despite efficient and comparable Arid1a knockdown in the different cohorts (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), the retained acinar cells observed in the E7 cohort failed to upregulate the ductal markers CK19 and Sox9 in the presence of mutant Kras (Figure 4G,H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4G and 4H.

claims.claim: Arid1a suppression accelerates the transition from an acinar to a mucinous cell fate in the presence of a pre-existing oncogenic Kras mutation.
claims.source: Thus, Arid1a suppression accelerates the transition from an acinar to a mucinous cell fate in the presence of a pre-existing oncogenic Kras mutation (adult and P5 cohorts) whereas, when occurring concomitant with KrasG12D activation, it paradoxically promotes retention of the acinar cell phenotype (E7 cohort).
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the temporal cohort experiments.

claims.claim: When Arid1a suppression occurs concomitant with KrasG12D activation, it paradoxically promotes retention of the acinar cell phenotype.
claims.source: Thus, Arid1a suppression accelerates the transition from an acinar to a mucinous cell fate in the presence of a pre-existing oncogenic Kras mutation (adult and P5 cohorts) whereas, when occurring concomitant with KrasG12D activation, it paradoxically promotes retention of the acinar cell phenotype (E7 cohort).
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the temporal cohort experiments.

claims.claim: Arid1a has a temporal, context-dependent role in regulating acinar identity in response to oncogenic Kras.
claims.source: Taken together, these data reveal a temporal, context-dependent role for Arid1a in regulating acinar identity in response to oncogenic Kras.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal cohort experiments.

claims.claim: Arid1a restoration did not reverse the acinar reprogramming phenotype.
claims.source: Remarkably, Arid1a restoration did not reverse the acinar reprogramming phenotype. As expected, pancreata from mice withdrawn from dox retained expression of the mKate2 lineage marker, but lost the shRNA-linked GFP fluorescence signal (Figure 5B). Staining of tissues from KC-RIK-shRen and -shArid1a animals for Arid1a showed partial restoration of Arid1a by 5 days after withdrawal and full restoration at 2 and 4 weeks (Figure 5C). Despite this, histological assessment of KC-RIK-shRen and -shArid1a mice after dox withdrawal showed retention of widespread mucinous lesions as in the on dox condition, without a reversal of the PanIN phenotype towards an acinar or even ADM cell fate (Figure 5D,E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by data from doxycycline withdrawal experiments shown in Figures 5B-E.

claims.claim: Arid1a loss enables a non-reversible reprogramming of cell fate that is dependent on cellular and genetic context.
claims.source: Thus, Arid1a loss enables a non-reversible reprogramming of cell fate that is dependent on cellular and genetic context.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the irreversibility experiments.

claims.claim: Principal component analysis of RNA-seq data indicated that the two shRNAs targeting Arid1a conferred a transcriptional profile distinct from that of the shRen animals.
claims.source: Principal component analysis of RNA-seq data indicated that the two shRNAs targeting Arid1a conferred a transcriptional profile distinct from that of the shRen animals, confirming these shRNAs triggered minimal off-target effects (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: The two Arid1a shRNAs triggered minimal off-target effects.
claims.source: Principal component analysis of RNA-seq data indicated that the two shRNAs targeting Arid1a conferred a transcriptional profile distinct from that of the shRen animals, confirming these shRNAs triggered minimal off-target effects (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the clustering of the two different Arid1a shRNAs together.

claims.claim: Analysis of RNAseq data detected 711 downregulated and 505 upregulated genes upon Arid1a knockdown.
claims.source: Further analysis of the RNAseq data using an FDR threshold of 0.05 detected 711 downregulated and 505 upregulated genes (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Notable changes upon Arid1a knockdown included a reduction in acinar-related digestive enzymes and an increase in cellular components needed for mucin production.
claims.source: Among the notable changes were a reduction in acinar-related digestive enzymes and an increase in cellular components needed for the mucin production characteristic of PDAC precursor lesions.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis.

claims.claim: Gene set enrichment analysis revealed a general activation of a mucinous lesion transcriptional program after 5 days on dox.
claims.source: Consistent with our histological findings, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed a general activation of a mucinous lesion transcriptional program after 5 days on dox: genes that are decreased in PanIN organoids relative to normal organoids were also downregulated, while genes enriched in PanIN organoids were up in shArid1a pancreata as well (Figure 6D) (Boj et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: GSEA identified downregulation of genes associated with acinar function upon Arid1a knockdown.
claims.source: In parallel with mucin upregulation characteristic of PanIN development in KC-RIK-shArid1a mice, GSEA identified downregulation of genes associated with acinar function, such as those encoding the digestive enzymes Cel, Klk1 and Amy1 (Hoang et al., 2016), which was confirmed by RT-PCR (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA and RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: Significant downregulation of gene expression programs sustained by master acinar TFs (Nr5a2 and Ptf1a) was noted upon Arid1a knockdown.
claims.source: Importantly, significant downregulation of gene expression programs sustained by master acinar TFs (Nr5a2 and Ptf1a) required to maintain acinar differentiation (Holmstrom et al., 2011; Jiang et al., 2016) (Figure 6D) were noted.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: RNA-seq data did not show significant downregulation of the acinar TFs Nr5a2, Ptf1a or Mist1 themselves at the 5-day timepoint.
claims.source: Interestingly, our RNA-seq data did not show significant downregulation of the acinar TFs Nr5a2, Ptf1a or Mist1 themselves at this timepoint (see Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The destabilization of acinar cell identity upon Arid1a suppression most likely results from impaired recruitment or function of acinar TFs at their appropriate targets.
claims.source: Thus, the destablization of acinar cell identity that occurs upon Arid1a suppression in the setting of oncogenic Kras most likely results from impaired recruitment or function of these acinar TFs at their appropriate targets.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that TF target genes are downregulated without changes in TF expression.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Arid1a resulted in striking changes in chromatin accessibility, with shArid1a chromatin profiles clearly separated from shRen by PCA.
claims.source: We found that knockdown of Arid1a resulted in striking changes in chromatin accessibility, with shArid1a chromatin profiles that clearly separated from shRen by PCA (Figure 7A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claims.claim: 50,000–60,000 dynamic peaks were observed upon Arid1a knockdown, virtually all of which were reduced in the shArid1a samples relative to the shRen controls.
claims.source: 50,000–60,000 dynamic peaks were observed, virtually all of which were reduced in the shArid1a samples relative to the shRen controls (Figure 7B,C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figures 7B and 7C.

claims.claim: Arid1a-containing SWI/SNF complexes are required to maintain substantial regions of open chromatin in the pre-neoplastic pancreas.
claims.source: This indicates that Arid1a-containing SWI/SNF complexes are required to maintain substantial regions of open chromatin in the pre-neoplastic pancreas.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the widespread loss of chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown.

claims.claim: The majority of dynamic sites upon Arid1a knockdown were located in intergenic regions or introns, while promoters displayed fewer dynamic peaks.
claims.source: Interestingly, although the chromatin accessibility was highest around transcriptional start site (TSS) regions (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), the majority of dynamic sites were located in intergenic regions or introns, while promoters displayed fewer dynamic peaks (relative to the genome-wide distribution of total detectable peaks) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The regions of reduced chromatin accessibility observed upon Arid1a knockdown likely include enhancers whose inactivation may be responsible for the altered transcriptional profiles.
claims.source: In B cells, intergenic and intronic regions that are enriched for Brg1 binding and lost upon Brg1 ablation are associated with H3K4me1 bound enhancers essential for establishing B-cell fate (Bossen et al., 2015). Accordingly, we suspect that the regions of reduced chromatin accessibility observed upon Arid1a knockdown includes enhancers, whose inactivation may be ultimately responsible for the altered transcriptional profiles we observed.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on published literature about SWI/SNF function in other cell types.

claims.claim: Binding motifs for several key acinar-specific TFs (Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Rbpj) were enriched in genomic regions losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown.
claims.source: In addition, and consistent with impact of Arid1a suppression on acinar cell fate, we identified enrichment of binding motifs for several key acinar-specific TFs (Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Rbpj) in the genomic regions losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: Binding motifs for Pdx1 were enriched in genomic regions losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown.
claims.source: These same sites also showed enrichment in binding motifs for Pdx1, a TF that constrains acinar identity during mutant Kras-driven PanIN development (Roy et al., 2016) (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: There was a significant enrichment of Nr5a2, Ptf1a, and Pdx1 binding sites at ATAC-seq peaks that lose accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown.
claims.source: This analysis showed a significant enrichment of TF binding sites at ATAC-seq peaks that lose accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown compared with sites without loss of acessibility (Nr5a2 and Ptf1a: p<2.2e-16, Pdx1: p<0.0016; Fisher's exact test; see Figure 7E and a representative ATAC-Seq track for the acinar target Cela2a).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7E.

claims.claim: Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Pdx1 target genes losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a suppression were significantly downregulated.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 7F, Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Pdx1 target genes losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a suppression were significantly downregulated in shArid1a vs. shRen mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 7F.

claims.claim: Genes downregulated upon Arid1a suppression showed a significantly increased density of Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Pdx1 binding sites losing chromatin accessibility compared to genes whose expression is upregulated or unchanged.
claims.source: More globally, genes downregulated upon Arid1a suppression showed a significantly increased density of Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Pdx1 binding sites losing chromatin accessibility as compared to genes whose expression is upregulated or unchanged (Figure 7G; Mean peak density: downregulated genes 1.53, upregulated genes: 0.72, unchanged: 0.92; Welch's t test: p=2.55e-14 for down vs. upregulated genes, p=6.372e-11 for down vs. unchanged genes).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 7G.

claims.claim: Arid1a depletion results in loss of chromatin accessibility at acinar-specific enhancers, limiting the transcriptional output of acinar master TFs and the expression of transcriptional programs that direct acinar cell fate.
claims.source: These data support a model whereby Arid1a depletion results in loss of chromatin accessibility at acinar-specific enhancers, limiting the transcriptional output of acinar master TFs and, consequently, the expression of transcriptional programs that direct acinar cell fate.
claims.evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from the combined ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: Suppression of Arid1a in adult acinar cells harboring oncogenic Kras mutations accelerates acinar to ductal reprogramming and specification of mucinous, pancreatic cancer precursor lesions.
claims.source: In this study, we used a rapid and robust mouse-modeling platform to study the consequences of inducible and reversible suppression of the Arid1a SWI/SNF subunit in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer. Suppression of Arid1a in adult acinar cells harboring oncogenic Kras mutations accelerates acinar to ductal reprogramming and specification of mucinous, pancreatic cancer precursor lesions that cannot be reversed by restoring endogenous Arid1a expression.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claims.claim: Mucinous pancreatic cancer precursor lesions induced by Arid1a suppression cannot be reversed by restoring endogenous Arid1a expression.
claims.source: Suppression of Arid1a in adult acinar cells harboring oncogenic Kras mutations accelerates acinar to ductal reprogramming and specification of mucinous, pancreatic cancer precursor lesions that cannot be reversed by restoring endogenous Arid1a expression.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the irreversibility findings.

claims.claim: Arid1a can provide a potent barrier to Kras driven acinar to ductal metaplasia and early stage pancreatic neoplasia.
claims.source: Thus, our data suggest that Arid1a can provide a potent barrier to Kras driven acinar to ductal metaplasia and, consequently, early stage pancreatic neoplasia.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claims.claim: Once disrupted by Arid1a mutation, altered cells are reprogrammed in such a manner that Arid1a is no longer needed to sustain the aberrant cell fate.
claims.source: Once disrupted by Arid1a mutation, these altered cells are reprogrammed in such a manner that Arid1a is no longer needed to sustain the aberrant cell fate.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the irreversibility experiments.

claims.claim: The phenotype produced by Arid1a depletion in the presence of oncogenic Kras is characterized by reduced chromatin accessibility accompanied by loss of acinar morphology, reduced expression of acinar genes, and upregulation of a signature characteristic of mucinous lesions.
claims.source: The phenotype produced by Arid1a depletion in the presence of an oncogenic Kras mutation is characterized by reduced chromatin accessibility accompanied by loss of acinar morphology, reduced expression of acinar genes, and upregulation of a signature characteristic of mucinous lesions.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the molecular and cellular phenotypes observed.

claims.claim: Genomic areas rendered accessible by Arid1a harbor elements involved in preventing acinar to duct like trans-differentiation in the context of mutant Kras.
claims.source: These features imply that genomic areas rendered accessible by Arid1a harbor elements involved in preventing acinar to duct like trans-differentiation in the context of mutant Kras, a critical rate-limiting step in Kras driven pancreatic neoplasia.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the chromatin accessibility and gene expression data.

claims.claim: Arid1a disruption, in the presence of oncogenic Kras, reduces the chromatin accessibility of key TFs to the enhancers of genes needed to sustain acinar cell fate.
claims.source: Indeed, our transcriptional and chromatin profiling data imply that Arid1a disruption, in the presence of oncogenic Kras, reduces the chromatin accessibility of key TFs to the enhancers of genes needed to sustain acinar cell fate.
claims.evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion drawn from the combined transcriptional and chromatin profiling data.

claims.claim: Nr5a2 can physically interact with the SWI/SNF complex via the Baf60 subunit.
claims.source: At least one such factor, Nr5a2, can physically interact with the SWI/SNF complex via the Baf60 subunit (Debril et al., 2004), suggesting a possible mechanism for aberrant Nr5a2 target deregulation upon Arid1a loss.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: The accelerated PanIN formation produced by Arid1a suppression required the presence of a Kras mutation.
claims.source: The accelerated PanIN formation produced by Arid1a suppression required the presence of a Kras mutation, the initiating event in pancreatic carcinogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing Arid1a effects in Kras mutant vs wild-type contexts.

claims.claim: Arid1a suppression in the normal pancreas did not appreciably perturb acinar differentiation, even during wound healing responses.
claims.source: Thus, Arid1a suppression in the normal pancreas did not appreciably perturb acinar differentiation, even during wound healing responses that force a reversible acinar to ductal metaplasia.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from experiments in the absence of Kras mutation.

claims.claim: Arid1a suppression sensitizes pancreatic epithelial cells to mucinous reprogramming by oncogenic Kras or increases the efficiency of Kras-induced acinar-to-ADM-to-PanIN transitions.
claims.source: Apparently, Arid1a suppression sensitizes pancreatic epithelial cells to mucinous reprogramming by oncogenic Kras or, alternatively, increases the efficiency of Kras-induced acinar-to-ADM-to-PanIN transitions.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the mechanism by which Arid1a loss cooperates with Kras.

claims.claim: The Kras-dependence of Arid1a suppression effects differs from the phenotype produced by deletion of acinar TFs such as Ptf1a or Nr5a2.
claims.source: Regardless, this Kras-dependence differs from the phenotype produced by deletion of acinar TFs such as Ptf1a or Nr5a2, whose loss generally perturbs acinar maintenance and/or regeneration (Cobo et al., 2018; Flandez et al., 2014a; Krah et al., 2015; von Figura et al., 2014b).
claims.evidence: This comparison is based on published literature about acinar TF deletions.

claims.claim: The potent and cooperative effects between oncogenic signaling and chromatin remodeling at eroding barriers to cellular plasticity contributes to the high frequency of SWI/SNF component inactivation in many cancer types.
claims.source: We hypothesize that the potent and cooperative effects between oncogenic signaling and chromatin remodeling at eroding barriers to cellular plasticity contributes to the high frequency of SWI/SNF component inactivation in many cancer types.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the findings of the study.

claims.claim: Deletion of Brg1 during pancreatic development in conjunction with oncogenic Kras results in the formation of IPMN-like lesions.
claims.source: Deletion of Brg1 during pancreatic development in conjunction with oncogenic Kras results in the formation of IPMN-like lesions contiguous with the native duct system that may derive from the ductal compartment rather than through ADM.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on published literature about Brg1 deletion.

claims.claim: Elimination of Brg1 in adult acinar cells prevents the development of Kras driven acinar to duct-like transdifferentiation and PanIN development.
claims.source: Furthermore elimination of Brg1 in adult acinar cells prevents the development of Kras driven acinar to duct-like transdifferentiation and PanIN development (von Figura et al., 2014a).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: The timing of SWI/SNF perturbation can have a dramatic effect on tumorigenesis phenotypes.

claims.source: Indeed, the inducible shRNA technology used herein has been optimized to produce gene suppression that approaches that produced by gene deletion (Bolden et al., 2014; Dow et al., 2015; Ebbesen et al., 2016; Hemann et al., 2003; Premsrirut et al., 2011) yet, by leaving the target locus intact, enables the endogenous protein to be re-expressed upon shRNA silencing.

Furthermore, they stand in contrast to what has been noted for other tumor suppressor genes, for example, in colon cancer models where reversible APC suppression promoted the expansion of undifferentiated cells that readily underwent differentiation upon APC restoration (Dow et al., 2015).

claims.claim: ARID1A controls the expression of thousands of gene targets via interaction with available TFs.

results.result: Postnatal Arid1a suppression in adult acinar cells with pre-existing KrasG12D mutations induces rapid, dramatic acinar-to-PanIN reprogramming characterized by loss of acinar markers, gain of mucinous lesion markers, and exocrine insufficiency, but does not frequently progress to PDAC.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C39 collectively demonstrate that acute Arid1a knockdown in adult KC-RIK mice causes rapid morbidity (C27-C31), dramatic pancreatic remodeling with PanIN formation (C32-C33), loss of acinar identity (C33-C35), but limited progression to PDAC (C36-C37). The data include survival curves, histology, immunofluorescence, and quantification from multiple independent shRNAs, providing strong convergent evidence for this major finding.

results.result: Arid1a is dispensable for maintaining normal acinar cell identity and regeneration in the absence of oncogenic Kras, but is specifically required to prevent Kras-driven preneoplastic transformation.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C48 demonstrate that Arid1a suppression in wild-type Kras mice (C-RIK) does not cause morbidity, maintains acinar markers, and does not impair pancreatitis-induced regeneration. This contrasts with the KC-RIK phenotype (C86-C87), establishing the Kras-dependence of Arid1a's role. The caerulein experiments provide rigorous functional validation of regenerative capacity.

results.result: The timing of Arid1a suppression relative to KrasG12D activation determines phenotypic outcome: embryonic suppression (E7) paradoxically promotes acinar cell retention, while postnatal suppression (P5 or adult) accelerates PanIN formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C55 demonstrate striking temporal context-dependence using three cohorts (E7, P5, adult). The E7 cohort shows retained Cpa1+ acinar tissue and failure to upregulate ductal markers (C51-C52), contrasting with P5/adult phenotypes (C50, C53-C54). This temporal effect is well-documented with histology and marker analysis, though the mechanistic basis remains unclear.

results.result: Arid1a-induced acinar-to-PanIN reprogramming is irreversible: restoration of endogenous Arid1a expression does not reverse the mucinous phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C57 demonstrate that doxycycline withdrawal restores Arid1a protein but does not reverse PanIN histology. This irreversibility is confirmed by multiple timepoints (5 days, 2 weeks, 4 weeks) and Alcian blue staining. The finding has important implications for tumor maintenance (C106) and is well-supported by the reversible shRNA system.

results.result: Arid1a suppression causes rapid transcriptional changes including downregulation of acinar genes and upregulation of mucinous lesion markers, with reduced expression of Nr5a2 and Ptf1a target genes despite unchanged TF expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C66 present RNA-seq data from sorted cells at 5 days post-dox showing 711 downregulated and 505 upregulated genes. PCA and clustering validate minimal off-target effects (C58-C59). GSEA confirms activation of PanIN signatures and downregulation of acinar programs (C62-C64). The observation that TF targets are downregulated without changes in TF expression (C65-C66) supports an indirect mechanism via chromatin accessibility.

results.result: Arid1a depletion causes widespread loss of chromatin accessibility (50,000-60,000 dynamic peaks), predominantly at intergenic/intronic regions enriched for acinar TF binding motifs (Nr5a2, Ptf1a, Pdx1), mechanistically linking chromatin changes to loss of acinar identity.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C77 present comprehensive ATAC-seq analysis showing dramatic chromatin closing upon Arid1a knockdown. The integration with ChIP-seq data demonstrates significant enrichment of acinar TF binding sites at regions losing accessibility (C74, p<2.2e-16), and these TF target genes are downregulated (C75-C76). The mechanistic model (C77, C84) is well-supported by the integrated genomic analyses.

results.result: Arid1a is a critical modulator of Kras-dependent changes in acinar cell identity, with timing and genetic context influencing the effects of SWI/SNF alterations in pancreatic tumorigenesis.
results.evaluation: These claims represent the overarching conclusions of the study, synthesizing the major findings about Arid1a's role as a barrier to Kras-driven transformation (C80, C104-C105) and the importance of temporal/genetic context (C5-C6). The conclusions are well-supported by the experimental data from multiple cohorts and molecular analyses.

results.result: Background context establishing that SWI/SNF mutations are common in cancer, have context-dependent roles, and that PDAC is initiated by KRAS mutations with acinar cell identity maintenance providing a barrier to tumorigenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C26 provide literature-based background establishing the prevalence of SWI/SNF mutations (C1, C9, C17), their context-dependent effects (C11-C15), PDAC biology (C18-C24), and the importance of acinar identity (C25-C26). All claims are supported by appropriate citations to published literature.

results.result: The accelerated PanIN phenotype observed with postnatal Arid1a suppression contrasts with prior studies showing that concurrent deletion of SWI/SNF subunits with Kras activation reduces PanIN formation, potentially due to timing differences or dosage effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C49, C91-C93 accurately cite prior literature showing different phenotypes with Brg1 or Arid1a deletion concurrent with Kras activation. The proposed explanations involving timing (C49, C95) or dosage effects (C94) are speculative but reasonable interpretations supported by the temporal cohort data.

results.result: Discussion of mechanistic possibilities (Nr5a2-SWI/SNF interaction), comparison to other TF deletions, implications for mouse modeling, and therapeutic considerations regarding context-specific dependencies.
results.evaluation: These claims represent speculative discussion points and broader implications. While C85 cites a known interaction, claims C88, C90, C94, C107 are explicitly speculative. Claims C96-C98 about mouse modeling limitations are reasonable inferences but not directly tested. The therapeutic implications (C107-C109) are forward-looking and would require additional validation.

results.result: Technical and methodological claims about the shRNA system, Cre specificity, and comparisons to other reversibility studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C99, C110, C112 are supported by citations describing the technical systems used. Claims C101-C103 provide appropriate literature context for the irreversibility findings. Claim C111 describes an observation about Cre specificity based on mKate2 staining patterns.
